name: What should homeowners ask a contractor before building a home office addition?

mainEntity.name: Which questions reveal whether a builder understands permits, design, timeline, and finish quality for office additions?
mainEntity.text: Which questions reveal whether a builder understands permits, design, timeline, and finish quality for office additions?

acceptedAnswer.text: The right contractor should be able to explain the project from concept to final inspection. Ask whether they have completed similar office additions in the same city, how they handle design and permitting, and what scope items are included in the price. It is also important to ask about site access, utility upgrades, insulation, HVAC, sound control, and finish quality, because office additions depend on more than framing and drywall. Homeowners should request a clear timeline with milestones, not just a single completion date. Change order handling matters too, because hidden conditions or design changes can affect budget quickly. A strong contractor will also discuss how the office will be used, since a client-facing space, a private work room, and a flexible guest room each require different design decisions. The best bids are not always the cheapest; they are the ones that show the contractor understands the entire process and the specific demands of the property.
acceptedAnswer.description: Homeowners should ask about permit experience, recent office addition projects, expected timeline, cost exclusions, structural and HVAC planning, and how change orders are handled. The best contractor can explain the process clearly and identify likely issues before construction starts.
